welcome.label: Welcome · the one-year jump

parts.label: ❓ The case question
parts.title: Did 1,275 manatees really show up in one year?
parts.body: Find 4 clues. Then crack the case on the Assignment tab.

welcome.script:
Hi, scientists! Last time, one fallen oak changed a whole forest. Today: how do scientists know if a whole ecosystem is healthy?

[ON SCREEN: Manatees from the air]
Every winter, scientists fly over Florida in small planes and count manatees. Those gray shapes? Manatees!

[ON SCREEN: Two flight logs]
Look at these two flight logs. 2009: 3,802. One year later: 5,077. That’s more than twelve hundred extra manatees in one year. Hmm. Manatees usually have one baby every few years.

[ON SCREEN: The case question]
So did that many really show up? Find the four clues. Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · count it or feel it? (Clue 1)

parts.label: ⚖ Two sides
parts.title: Count it or feel it?
rows: A scientist can count or measure it.

parts.label: 👆 How to play
parts.title: One card at a time
rows: Drag it to a side, or tap a side.
Then list three things you could measure.

warmup.script:
(Step outside or look out a window.) Is it a nice day? I think so. But you might not! That’s a feeling.

How many clouds are in the sky? That we can count.

[ON SCREEN: Two sides]
Scientists trust things they can count or measure, not feelings.

[ON SCREEN: How to play]
Read each card about two Florida wetlands. Drag it to the side it belongs on, or tap the side. Then list three things a scientist could measure. Press Listen. Dr. Reyes has a field secret for you.

part2.label: Part 2 · fly the survey (Clue 2)

parts.label: 🛩 The practice flight
parts.title: Same 200 manatees every flight
rows: Fly, then change ONE thing and fly again.

part2.script:
[ON SCREEN: Manatees in a warm spring]
When the water gets cold, manatees crowd into warm springs like this one. Easy to count! On warm days they spread out all over.

[ON SCREEN: The practice flight]
Now you fly. Two hundred manatees live near this spring, every single day. Pick the weather and the wind, then fly. Write down your count. Now change just one thing and fly again.

Did the manatees change, or did your count? That’s Clue 2. Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

explore.label: Part 4 · thirty years of counts (Clue 4)

parts.label: 📈 Every flight
parts.title: Thirty years of dots
parts.body: The dashed line shows the trend: which way the numbers go over many years.

explore.script:
(Hold up one sock.) If I find one sock on the floor, is my room messy? Maybe! I need more evidence.

[ON SCREEN: Two dots]
This chart starts with just two survey flights, one year apart. Up or down? Decide.

[ON SCREEN: Every flight]
Then press Show every flight. Thirty years of real dots! Some years jump, some dip. The dashed line shows the trend, the way the numbers move over many years.

That’s your last clue. Press Listen.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: Did 1,275 manatees really show up?
parts.body: Pick the answer that fits all four clues.

parts.label: ✍️ Your case report
parts.title: Four places to work
rows: Copy your Gathered Answers into Canvas

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
You found all four clues! Crack the case at the top of this tab. Did twelve hundred manatees really appear in one year?

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Then your case report: two short answers, a graph, and a CER.

[ON SCREEN: Part C graph]
In Part C, you build the graph. Tap in each column to set the dot at the right height. Then write one sentence: which way did the numbers go?

Stuck? Press Hint under any box. Press Listen on the walkie-talkie.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The quote
parts.title: Some people say…
parts.body: “Invasive species like Burmese pythons are no big deal. Florida has plenty of native animals.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
[ON SCREEN: A Burmese python]
This snake is not from Florida. It came from Asia.

[ON SCREEN: The quote]
Some people say invasive species are no big deal, because Florida has plenty of native animals. Hmm. Do you agree?

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Remember CER. Tap your side, then two facts from the lesson. Numbers make strong evidence! Then explain how your facts prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…”

Press Listen. Dr. Reyes wants to hear your side.

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🐚 Your specimen
parts.title: Florida apple snail shell
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next time
parts.title: Inside out
parts.body: Body parts that help Florida plants and animals survive.

closing.script:
Case closed! One count can fool you. Many years of counts tell the truth.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist and a Florida apple snail shell goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next time]
Next time, we zoom in. Why does a spoonbill have a flat, spoon-shaped beak? We’ll find out how body parts help living things survive.

Press Listen for Dr. Reyes’s last word.

part3.label: Part 3 · four Florida stories (Clue 3)
part3.script:
[ON SCREEN: A Florida manatee]
Four Florida stories, four case files. Read each one, stamp it Recovering or Out of balance, then find the line that proves it. Careful: some lines are true but don’t prove anything. Press Listen.

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.

vr.label: VR activity · Two plots (separate page)

parts.label: 🧭 Two ways
parts.title: Two ways to do it
rows: VR Field Mission: build a healthy plot and a hog plot in Tranquil Forest.
No headset? Count both photo plots on your computer.

parts.label: 🥇 The badge
parts.title: Balance Scale badge
parts.body: Save your capture in VR to earn it.

vr.script:
Hi, scientists! You cracked the manatee case. Now Dr. Reyes has a new question.

[ON SCREEN: The wild hogs]
Wild hogs moved into the forest across the creek. (Hold up two fingers.) Two patches of forest. Which one is in balance? Remember: count it, don’t feel it.

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]
Pick your way at the top. With a headset, go into the Tranquil Forest and build two plots: a healthy one with lots of different living things, and one the hogs took over. No headset? Count both photo plots on your computer.

[ON SCREEN: The badge]
Finish in VR and you earn the Balance Scale badge!

Press Listen on Dr. Reyes’s walkie-talkie, right below me.
